findings.problem: CSH-01 must propagate mandatory preparation failure through public install, but install-kit.sh is not owned until CSH-03 and currently swallows preparation failure with || true. The first task cannot satisfy its assigned E2E obligation within ownership.
findings.minimal_fix: Add _ask/scripts/install-kit.sh to CSH-01 owned_paths; retain sequential ownership in CSH-03. Include bootstrap propagation in the focused caller check.

findings.problem: CSH-T07 is classified as a passing regression but includes launcher help and no startup writes. Current askit automatically invokes completion installation for completion/help and delegates help to an existing project dispatcher. That combines new CSH-001 behavior with the existing --complete guard and would bypass required Red for the new portion.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep a narrow --complete completion guard as regression; move launcher help and startup-edit refusal into the new-behavior T08 or another explicitly new case. Establish the actual old guard baseline during authorized implementation; do not claim it has passed now.

findings.location: plan.md: CSH-10 and Verification approach; test-plan.json: CSH-T38/CSH-T39
findings.problem: The two composed journeys are marked new and authored only in the last task after all relevant behavior has been implemented by CSH-01 through CSH-09. The plan requires Red at each owning task but supplies no way to obtain genuine preimplementation Red for these final journeys. A successful earlier implementation would make those new tests Green on arrival.
findings.minimal_fix: Define an executable baseline capture strategy for these exact journey assertions before earlier production changes, with coordinator/TaskGraph ownership and accepted-contract evidence preserved, or redesign test/task placement so their genuine behavior Red precedes the relevant implementation. Do not relabel new aggregate feature behavior as regression merely to bypass Red, weaken assertions, or introduce artificial failure.
